name: Volunteer Project Detail - Full Description No Photo

projects.blurb: Help promote HIT events from start to finish by creating and scheduling engaging social media content before, during, and after each event. This project is ideal for a volunteer who enjoys event marketing, storytelling, and turning event recordings into reusable content.
projects.body:
For this specific New York event, the volunteer will support the full social media promotion cycle, including:

- Develop a social media content plan and posting schedule for before, during, and after the event.
- Write engaging LinkedIn posts that align with HIT's brand, audience, and event goals.
- Create promotional posts announcing the event, speakers, panelists, partners, and key discussion topics.
- Develop a LinkedIn tagging strategy for speakers, panelists, sponsors, partners, volunteers, and relevant organizations to increase visibility and engagement.
- Coordinate with featured individuals to confirm their correct LinkedIn profiles and company pages.
- Create supporting content, such as speaker spotlights, quotes, polls, discussion questions, countdown posts, and attendee-engagement posts.
- Prepare suggested social copy that speakers, partners, and HIT leaders can share with their own networks.
- Create or coordinate social media graphics and ensure that each post includes the correct links, tags, event details, and calls to action.
- Monitor engagement and respond to or flag relevant comments and questions.
- Capture or coordinate real-time event content, when possible.
- Create post-event recap and thank-you posts.
- Repurpose event photos, videos, audio, quotes, and key takeaways into at least six additional pieces of content that can be shared throughout the year.

Review post performance and provide a brief summary of results, insights, and recommendations for future events.
projects.title: Social Media Marketing Specialist- Events

description: The real entry an editor created in the CMS, rendered at its own URL, with the collection in the state it is actually in today: exactly one project. That makes this the scenario for both of the feature's do-nothing branches. The header shows a time commitment and NO date range, because this entry has neither date - and it must be pixel-identical to what it rendered before dates existed, with no empty gap under the title. And the page simply ends at the sign-up CTA: with no other open project to offer there is no 'You may also be interested in' section and no heading, which is the common case right now rather than an edge case. Her entry also carries no photo and no sign-up link of its own, so it still shows the two older fallbacks - no empty photo band, and the site-wide volunteer CTA standing in for a missing form. Captured at Desktop only: below 1040px the site's nav expands every dropdown inline by design, so a mobile full-page shot is all nav and no page - the mobile layout of this page is covered by the VolunteerProjectPage component scenario instead.
